metadata.source: Kaggle Open Source Healthcare Datasets (Disease & Symptoms Prediction, Disease Precaution & Description, MedQuAD Clinical FAQ)

emergencyKeywords: i think i am having a heart attack

conditions.name: Acute Myocardial Infarction (Heart Attack)
conditions.description: Sudden blockage of blood flow to the heart muscle, requiring immediate emergency medical care.
precautions: Call 112 / 108 immediately — do not drive yourself
Chew one 325mg regular aspirin if not allergic and no contraindications
Sit resting in a comfortable upright position
Loosen tight clothing around the neck and chest
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency — Call 112 / 108 immediately. Every minute matters.

conditions.name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
conditions.description: Persistently elevated arterial blood pressure that increases long-term heart disease and stroke risk.
precautions: Follow the DASH diet (sodium under 2,000 mg/day, rich in potassium)
Engage in 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise weekly
Monitor blood pressure daily at rest with a validated arm cuff
Avoid tobacco and limit alcohol consumption
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Seek emergency care if BP exceeds 180/120 mmHg with chest pain, vision changes, or shortness of breath.

conditions.name: Hyperlipidemia (High Cholesterol)
conditions.description: Excess lipids and LDL cholesterol in the bloodstream that build arterial plaque over time.
precautions: Replace saturated and trans fats with olive oil, nuts, and avocados
Increase soluble dietary fiber (oats, beans, lentils, psyllium husk)
Engage in routine aerobic exercise to raise HDL (good cholesterol)
Get fasting lipid profile checked annually
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult your doctor for formal lipid panel testing and cardiovascular risk assessment.

conditions.name: Cardiac Arrhythmia & Palpitations
conditions.description: Irregular, abnormally fast (tachycardia) or slow (bradycardia) heart rhythms.
precautions: Reduce caffeine, energy drinks, nicotine, and alcohol intake
Practice slow diaphragmatic breathing during stress-induced episodes
Ensure balanced electrolyte intake (potassium, magnesium) from whole foods
Keep a daily log of triggers and episode durations
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Seek emergency evaluation if palpitations occur with chest pain, fainting (syncope), or severe shortness of breath.

conditions.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
conditions.description: A metabolic disorder caused by insulin resistance leading to elevated chronic blood glucose levels.
precautions: Follow a low-glycemic, fiber-rich, portion-controlled meal plan
Walk for 15-20 minutes after main meals to lower postprandial glucose spikes
Inspect feet daily for cuts, blisters, or pressure sores
Schedule HbA1c testing every 3-6 months
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Contact doctor if blood sugar exceeds 250 mg/dL or if experiencing nausea, confusion, and fruity-smelling breath.

conditions.name: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
conditions.description: An autoimmune condition where the pancreas produces little to no insulin.
precautions: Adhere strictly to daily insulin therapy prescribed by an endocrinologist
Monitor blood glucose multiple times daily or use a continuous glucose monitor (CGM)
Always carry fast-acting carbohydrates (glucose tablets, juice) for hypoglycemia
Test for ketones if blood glucose is persistently above 240 mg/dL
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency care needed for persistent vomiting, rapid breathing, confusion, or severe hypoglycemia unresponsive to sugar.

conditions.name: Hypothyroidism (Underactive Thyroid)
conditions.description: Underactive thyroid gland producing insufficient T3/T4 hormones, slowing overall body metabolism.
precautions: Take prescribed Levothyroxine on an empty stomach with water, 30-60 minutes before breakfast
Avoid taking calcium or iron supplements within 4 hours of thyroid medicine
Maintain a nutrient-dense diet rich in selenium and zinc
Get regular serum TSH and Free T4 blood tests
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See an endocrinologist if fatigue worsens, neck swelling (goiter) develops, or heart rate drops unusually low.

conditions.name: Hyperthyroidism (Overactive Thyroid)
conditions.description: Overactive thyroid gland producing excess thyroid hormones, accelerating metabolism.
precautions: Avoid excess iodine (kelp, high-iodine dietary supplements)
Stay hydrated and avoid high caffeine intake
Incorporate stress reduction practices to calm sympathetic nervous tone
Monitor resting pulse rate daily
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult an endocrinologist immediately if experiencing high fever, rapid pulse (>140 bpm), or agitation (Thyroid Storm risk).

conditions.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
conditions.description: A hormonal disorder causing enlarged ovaries with small cysts, insulin resistance, and menstrual irregularity.
precautions: Adopt a low-glycemic, anti-inflammatory whole-food diet to manage insulin resistance
Incorporate regular strength training and brisk walking to improve insulin sensitivity
Prioritize 7-8 hours of quality sleep and manage cortisol/stress
Maintain regular gynecological and metabolic checkups
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a gynecologist or endocrinologist for ultrasound diagnosis and personalized hormonal management.

conditions.name: Gout (Uric Acid Arthritis)
conditions.description: Painful inflammatory arthritis caused by high uric acid crystals depositing in joints, most commonly the big toe.
precautions: Drink 2.5-3 liters of water daily to help kidneys flush uric acid
Limit high-purine foods (organ meats, red meat, shellfish, beer)
Avoid high-fructose corn syrup and sugary soft drinks
Apply cold ice packs wrapped in a towel during acute flares
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a doctor for prescription anti-inflammatory therapy and serum uric acid level testing.

conditions.name: Bronchial Asthma
conditions.description: Chronic inflammatory airway disease causing episodic wheezing, chest tightness, and breathlessness.
symptoms: dry cough at night or early morning
shortness of breath during exertion or cold air
precautions: Always carry a fast-acting prescribed rescue inhaler (e.g. Albuterol)
Avoid known triggers: dust mites, pet dander, cigarette smoke, strong perfumes
Use a spacer device with your inhaler for optimal lung delivery
Follow a written Asthma Action Plan prepared with your doctor
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency if rescue inhaler fails after 15 mins, or if lips turn pale/blue or speaking full sentences is impossible.

conditions.name: Acute Bronchitis
conditions.description: Temporary inflammation of the bronchial airway lining, typically following a viral cold.
symptoms: persistent cough with clear or colored phlegm
precautions: Drink plenty of warm liquids (herbal tea, broth, warm water with honey)
Use a cool-mist room humidifier to loosen respiratory mucus
Avoid cigarette smoke, cold dry air, and airborne irritants
Understand that viral bronchitis does not benefit from antibiotics
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor if cough lasts longer than 3 weeks, produces rust-colored blood, or is accompanied by high fever.

conditions.name: Pneumonia (Lung Infection)
conditions.description: Infection that inflames air sacs (alveoli) in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus.
symptoms: cough with green, yellow, or bloody mucus
sharp chest pain when breathing deeply
precautions: Rest in bed and stay well hydrated with electrolyte fluids
Take all prescribed antibiotics or antivirals exactly as directed by your physician
Use a fingertip pulse oximeter to monitor oxygen saturation (normal is ≥ 95%)
Get vaccinated against Pneumococcal bacteria and Influenza
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Immediate medical attention needed if experiencing difficulty breathing, chest pain, blue lips, or SpO2 < 92%.

conditions.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
conditions.description: Progressive, chronic inflammatory lung disease causing obstructed airflow from the lungs.
symptoms: chronic cough with daily sputum production
precautions: Strictly eliminate all smoking and exposure to secondhand smoke or biomass fuel
Use prescribed bronchodilator/corticosteroid maintenance inhalers daily
Practice pursed-lip breathing exercises to improve ventilation efficiency
Stay current on annual flu and pneumonia vaccinations
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Seek urgent medical care if breathlessness suddenly worsens or sputum turns thick and dark green/brown.

conditions.name: Common Cold (Viral Upper Respiratory Infection)
conditions.description: A self-limiting viral infection of the nose, sinuses, and throat, usually caused by rhinoviruses.
precautions: Rest and drink abundant warm water, soups, and herbal teas
Use saline nasal sprays or saline sinus rinses to clear congestion
Gargle warm salt water (1/2 tsp salt in 1 cup warm water) for sore throat relief
Wash hands frequently to avoid spreading virus to others
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor if symptoms worsen after 10 days, or if accompanied by high fever (>102°F) or earache.

conditions.name: Influenza (Flu)
conditions.description: A contagious viral infection with sudden onset of high fever, body aches, and prostration.
precautions: Get abundant bed rest and isolate at home until fever-free for 24 hours
Hydrate aggressively with warm water, broths, and electrolyte drinks
Take acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever/aches as advised by a pharmacist
Get an annual flu vaccine each autumn
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Seek prompt medical care for shortness of breath, persistent chest pain, confusion, or if high-risk (elderly, pregnant).

conditions.name: Sinusitis (Sinus Infection)
conditions.description: Inflammation and swelling of tissue lining the sinuses, causing blocked nasal drainage and facial pressure.
symptoms: facial pain and pressure around eyes, cheeks, and forehead
precautions: Inhale warm steam from a bowl of hot water or take hot showers
Perform sterile saline nasal irrigations (Neti pot with distilled water)
Apply warm compresses over forehead and nasal bridges
Stay hydrated and sleep with head elevated
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor if symptoms persist over 10 days, cause severe one-sided facial swelling, or high fever develops.

conditions.name: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever)
conditions.description: Allergic inflammation of the nasal passages triggered by airborne allergens like pollen, dust mites, or mold.
symptoms: itchy roof of mouth or ears
precautions: Keep windows closed during high pollen counts and use air purifiers with HEPA filters
Wash bed linens weekly in hot water (>130°F / 54°C)
Rinse nasal passages daily with isotonic saline spray
Use non-drowsy second-generation antihistamines or steroid nasal sprays as advised by pharmacist
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult an allergist if symptoms disrupt daily life, sleep, or trigger asthma symptoms.

conditions.name: COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2)
conditions.description: Contagious viral respiratory illness causing symptoms from mild cold-like illness to viral pneumonia.
precautions: Isolate and test using an at-home rapid antigen test upon symptom onset
Monitor blood oxygen levels with a pulse oximeter (normal ≥ 95%)
Stay well hydrated and rest in a well-ventilated room
Stay up-to-date with recommended booster vaccines
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency if breathing is labored, chest pressure is persistent, lips turn blue, or SpO2 drops below 92%.

conditions.name: GERD & Acid Reflux
conditions.description: Chronic condition where stomach acid flows back into the esophagus, causing mucosal irritation.
symptoms: burning sensation in chest after eating (heartburn)
precautions: Avoid lying down for at least 3 hours after meals
Elevate head of bed 6 inches using bed risers or a wedge pillow
Reduce trigger foods: citrus, tomatoes, chocolate, caffeine, mint, fried and spicy dishes
Eat smaller, frequent meals rather than heavy dinners
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a doctor if swallowing is painful/difficult, weight loss occurs, or if chest pain is accompanied by left arm/jaw pain.

conditions.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
conditions.description: Open sores that develop on the inside lining of the stomach (gastric) or upper small intestine (duodenal), often caused by H. pylori bacteria or NSAIDs.
symptoms: burning stomach pain between meals or at night
precautions: Avoid regular use of NSAID painkillers (ibuprofen, aspirin, naproxen)
Eliminate tobacco smoke and reduce alcohol consumption
Eat regular balanced meals and avoid skipping meals
Consult your physician for H. pylori stool or breath testing
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Immediate care needed if vomiting blood/coffee-ground material, or passing black tarry stools (melena).

conditions.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
conditions.description: A common functional gastrointestinal disorder affecting the large intestine with cramping, bloating, and altered bowel habits.
symptoms: abdominal cramping relieved after bowel movement
precautions: Adopt a Low-FODMAP diet under dietary supervision to identify food triggers
Increase soluble fiber (oats, psyllium) while moderating insoluble fiber
Practice stress reduction (mindfulness, yoga) to regulate gut-brain axis
Stay hydrated and avoid carbonated beverages and artificial sweeteners
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a doctor if experiencing unexplained weight loss, rectal bleeding, or persistent nocturnal diarrhea.

conditions.name: Acute Gastroenteritis (Stomach Flu & Food Poisoning)
conditions.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines typically caused by viral or bacterial infection from contaminated food/water.
precautions: Rehydrate sip-by-sip with Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) solution and clear broths
Follow the BRAT diet (Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast) as nausea settles
Avoid dairy, caffeine, alcohol, fatty foods, and spicy seasonings for 48 hours
Rest and wash hands thoroughly with soap to prevent transmission
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Seek medical evaluation if unable to keep fluids down for 24 hours, diarrhea lasts > 3 days, or high fever/blood in stool occurs.

conditions.name: Chronic Constipation
conditions.description: Infrequent bowel movements (fewer than 3 per week) or difficulty passing hard, dry stools.
precautions: Increase dietary fiber gradually to 25-35 grams daily (whole grains, prunes, chia seeds, vegetables)
Drink 2-3 liters of water throughout the day
Engage in regular daily physical movement to stimulate colonic motility
Never ignore the natural urge to have a bowel movement
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor if constipation is sudden, accompanied by severe abdominal pain, vomiting, or blood in stool.

conditions.name: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD)
conditions.description: Accumulation of excess fat in liver cells in individuals who drink little to no alcohol, closely tied to metabolic syndrome.
symptoms: vague dull discomfort in upper right abdomen
precautions: Achieve a gradual 7-10% body weight reduction through calorie-controlled whole-food diet
Eliminate refined sugars, high-fructose corn syrup, and sweetened beverages
Engage in regular aerobic exercise and resistance training
Get regular liver enzyme (ALT/AST) blood tests and liver ultrasound
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a gastroenterologist/hepatologist for fibrosis staging and comprehensive metabolic management.

conditions.name: Gallstones (Cholelithiasis)
conditions.description: Hardened deposits of digestive fluid that form in the gallbladder and may block bile ducts.
symptoms: sudden intensifying pain in upper right abdomen
pain radiating to right shoulder or back
precautions: Adopt a low-fat, high-fiber Mediterranean diet
Avoid crash diets and rapid weight loss which increase gallstone formation
Maintain regular meal times and avoid prolonged fasting
Stay hydrated throughout the day
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency evaluation needed if pain lasts > 4 hours, or if accompanied by high fever, chills, or yellowing of eyes/skin (jaundice).

conditions.name: Migraine Headache
conditions.description: A neurological condition manifesting as recurrent, pulsating, one-sided headaches often with sensory sensitivity and nausea.
precautions: Rest in a quiet, dark room during acute attacks
Apply cold ice packs to forehead or back of neck
Maintain a headache trigger diary (sleep, stress, skipped meals, aged cheese, MSG)
Stay consistently hydrated throughout the day
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency if sudden 'thunderclap' headache occurs (worst of life in seconds) or if accompanied by fever, stiff neck, or weakness.

conditions.name: Tension-Type Headache
conditions.description: The most common headache, characterized by a dull, aching band-like pressure around the forehead and scalp.
symptoms: dull aching head pain on both sides
tenderness on scalp, neck, and shoulder muscles
precautions: Apply warm compresses to neck and shoulders to relax tense muscles
Practice screen breaks (20-20-20 rule) and optimize ergonomic desk posture
Engage in stress relief: slow deep breathing, meditation, or light walking
Stay hydrated and avoid skipping meals
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor if headaches occur more than 15 days per month or wake you from sleep.

conditions.name: Vertigo & BPPV (Inner Ear Dizziness)
conditions.description: A sensation that you or your environment is spinning, most often caused by inner ear calcium crystals dislodging (BPPV).
symptoms: spinning sensation triggered by head position changes
precautions: Sit down immediately upon dizziness onset to prevent falls
Avoid sudden head movements or rapidly looking upwards
Perform Epley canalith repositioning maneuver under healthcare guidance
Keep walkways well-lit and free of tripping hazards
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency if vertigo is accompanied by double vision, slurred speech, facial weakness, or arm numbness (Stroke signs).

conditions.name: Sciatica (Lumbar Radiculopathy)
conditions.description: Pain radiating along the sciatic nerve pathway from the lower back through the hip, buttock, and down one leg.
symptoms: sharp or burning pain radiating down back of leg
numbness or tingling in foot or toes
pain worsened by prolonged sitting or coughing
precautions: Alternate cold ice packs (first 48 hours) and warm heating pads
Engage in gentle hamstring and piriformis stretches
Avoid prolonged bed rest; maintain gentle walking as tolerated
Use lumbar support while sitting and avoid heavy lifting
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency if you experience sudden loss of bowel or bladder control, or progressive severe leg weakness (Cauda Equina Syndrome).

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis
conditions.description: Wear-and-tear degradation of joint cartilage and underlying bone, commonly affecting knees, hips, and hands.
symptoms: joint pain during or after movement
morning joint stiffness lasting under 30 minutes
precautions: Engage in low-impact joint-friendly exercises: swimming, cycling, walking
Maintain a healthy body weight to reduce mechanical load on weight-bearing joints
Use warm baths/compresses for stiffness and cold packs for acute inflammation
Wear cushioned supportive footwear
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult an orthopedic doctor if joint becomes hot, red, and swollen, or if pain severely limits daily walking.

conditions.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)
conditions.description: An autoimmune inflammatory disorder where the immune system attacks joint linings, causing symmetric swelling and bone erosion.
symptoms: symmetrical joint involvement (both wrists or hands)
prolonged morning stiffness lasting over 1 hour
precautions: Work with a rheumatologist for early Disease-Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drug (DMARD) therapy
Engage in gentle range-of-motion exercises to maintain joint mobility
Follow an anti-inflammatory diet rich in Omega-3 fatty acids (flaxseeds, walnuts, fatty fish)
Balance active periods with adequate rest during flare-ups
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a rheumatologist promptly upon experiencing persistent symmetric joint swelling to prevent permanent joint damage.

conditions.name: Acute Lower Back Pain (Lumbago)
conditions.description: Pain in the lumbar spine area, commonly resulting from muscle strain, ligament sprain, or poor lifting mechanics.
symptoms: dull ache or sharp pain in lower back
precautions: Stay gently active with light walking; avoid prolonged bed rest over 24 hours
Apply ice packs for the first 48 hours, followed by warm compresses
Practice safe lifting technique: bend at the knees, not the waist, keeping load close to body
Perform gentle pelvic tilts and core-strengthening exercises once acute pain subsides
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor if pain radiates past the knee, causes leg numbness/weakness, or is accompanied by fever or bladder dysfunction.

conditions.name: Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis)
conditions.description: Stiffness, pain, and limited range of motion in the shoulder joint capsule that develops gradually.
symptoms: dull aching shoulder pain worse at night
inability to reach overhead or behind back
precautions: Perform daily gentle pendulum exercises and passive stretching under physical therapy guidance
Apply warm heat before stretching exercises to loosen joint capsule
Avoid completely immobilizing the arm in a sling
Manage blood glucose carefully, as diabetes significantly increases frozen shoulder risk
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult an orthopedic specialist or physical therapist for guided mobilization therapy.

conditions.name: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema)
conditions.description: Chronic inflammatory skin condition causing dry, intensely itchy, red, and irritated skin patches.
symptoms: red to brownish-gray patches on creases of elbows, knees, or neck
precautions: Apply thick ceramide-rich moisturizers within 3 minutes of lukewarm bathing
Take short, lukewarm showers and avoid harsh fragranced soaps
Wear breathable, loose cotton clothing and avoid scratchy wool
Keep fingernails trimmed short to prevent skin trauma and infection from scratching
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a dermatologist if skin becomes hot, oozes honey-colored fluid, or shows signs of bacterial infection.

conditions.name: Psoriasis
conditions.description: An autoimmune skin disease that speeds up the life cycle of skin cells, leading to thick red patches covered with silvery scales.
symptoms: raised red skin plaques covered with thick silvery scales
dry cracked skin that may bleed
precautions: Moisturize skin heavily with ointments or thick creams daily
Get brief, controlled sunlight exposure as advised by dermatologist
Avoid known flare triggers: skin injury, stress, smoking, heavy alcohol
Take daily lukewarm baths with Epsom salt or colloidal oatmeal
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a dermatologist for prescription topical, phototherapy, or biologic therapy options.

conditions.name: Acne Vulgaris
conditions.description: A common skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil (sebum) and dead skin cells.
precautions: Wash face twice daily with a gentle, non-comedogenic cleanser
Never pop, squeeze, or pick at blemishes to prevent scarring and infection
Use water-based, non-comedogenic sunscreen and cosmetics
Over-the-counter benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid can be used as directed by pharmacist
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a dermatologist if over-the-counter products fail after 8-12 weeks or if developing deep cystic scars.

conditions.name: Fungal Skin Infection (Ringworm / Tinea / Athlete's Foot)
conditions.description: Superficial fungal infection of the skin, scalp, groin (jock itch), or feet (athlete's foot).
symptoms: ring-shaped red itchy rash with raised borders
intense itching and burning in groin or feet
mild hair loss in affected scalp areas
precautions: Keep affected skin areas clean, dry, and cool
Wear loose, breathable cotton clothing and change socks daily
Do not share towels, combs, clothing, or personal hygiene items
Apply over-the-counter topical antifungal cream (Clotrimazole, Terbinafine) as advised by pharmacist for full course
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor if rash does not improve after 2 weeks of OTC topical treatment, or if widespread.

conditions.name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
conditions.description: Bacterial infection in any part of the urinary tract, most commonly the bladder and urethra.
symptoms: burning pain or stinging during urination (dysuria)
frequent urgent need to urinate with little output
precautions: Drink 2.5-3 liters of water daily to flush bacteria from the urinary system
Urinate promptly when the urge arises; do not hold urine for prolonged periods
Always wipe from front to back after using the toilet
Urinate shortly after sexual intercourse
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Seek prompt medical care for antibiotic prescription, or emergency care if experiencing high fever, chills, nausea, or flank/back pain (Kidney infection).

conditions.name: Dengue Fever
conditions.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes in tropical and subtropical regions.
symptoms: severe headache and pain behind the eyes
intense muscle and joint pain ('breakbone fever')
precautions: Hydrate intensively with Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS), coconut water, and fluids
Take Paracetamol/Acetaminophen for fever; strictly avoid Aspirin and Ibuprofen (they increase bleeding risk)
Monitor platelet count daily through complete blood count (CBC) testing
Rest completely and use mosquito nets to prevent secondary transmission
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency warning signs: severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums/nose, extreme fatigue, or sudden drop in platelet count (Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever).

conditions.name: Typhoid Fever
conditions.description: A bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, transmitted through contaminated food or drinking water.
precautions: Drink only boiled, purified, or bottled water
Eat thoroughly cooked, piping-hot foods; avoid raw street food and unpeeled fruits
Take the full course of prescribed antibiotics even after fever resolves
Wash hands thoroughly with soap before eating and preparing food
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor immediately for blood culture/Widal test confirmation and appropriate antibiotic prescription.

conditions.name: Malaria
conditions.description: A life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
symptoms: cyclical high fever with shaking chills (rigors)
precautions: Undergo rapid diagnostic blood testing (malaria smear/RDT) immediately upon fever onset in endemic zones
Complete full course of prescribed Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT)
Sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs)
Use mosquito repellent creams (DEET) and eliminate standing water around living areas
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Immediate hospital evaluation required for prompt parasite testing and anti-malarial treatment.

conditions.name: Generalized Anxiety & Panic Episodes
conditions.description: Mental health conditions characterized by persistent excessive worry, autonomic arousal, or sudden surges of intense panic.
symptoms: feeling of choking or shortness of breath
precautions: Practice diaphragmatic box breathing (inhale 4s, hold 4s, exhale 4s, hold 4s) during acute spikes
Apply the 5-4-3-2-1 grounding technique to reconnect with the physical environment
Gradually reduce caffeine, energy drinks, and nicotine intake
Engage with licensed mental health professionals for Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: If experiencing physical symptoms for the first time, rule out cardiac causes with a doctor. For self-harm thoughts, call 14416 (Tele-MANAS) or 112 immediately.

conditions.name: Major Depressive Disorder (Depression)
conditions.description: A mood disorder causing persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness, and loss of interest in daily activities.
precautions: Establish small, manageable daily routines (e.g. 15-minute morning walk in sunlight)
Stay connected with trusted family members, friends, or support communities
Prioritize regular sleep hygiene and avoid alcohol and substance use
Consult a licensed psychiatrist or psychologist for evidence-based psychotherapy
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Immediate help: If having thoughts of self-harm or suicide, contact Tele-MANAS (14416 / 1800-891-4416) or emergency services (112) immediately.

conditions.name: Chronic Insomnia & Sleep Disorders
conditions.description: Persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or achieving restorative quality sleep.
symptoms: waking up during the night or too early
precautions: Maintain a fixed sleep and wake schedule every day, including weekends
Eliminate screen exposure (phones, tablets, TV) at least 60 minutes before bed
Keep bedroom cool, completely dark, and quiet
Avoid caffeine after 2:00 PM and avoid heavy late dinners
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a sleep specialist if insomnia lasts > 3 months and impairs daytime functioning.

conditions.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
conditions.description: Condition where blood lacks adequate healthy red blood cells due to insufficient iron needed for hemoglobin synthesis.
symptoms: unusual cravings for ice or starch (pica)
shortness of breath on light exertion
precautions: Consume iron-rich foods: lean meat, beans, dark leafy greens, lentils, fortified cereals
Pair plant-based iron with Vitamin C sources (citrus, tomatoes) to multiply absorption
Avoid drinking tea or coffee with iron-rich meals (tannins block absorption)
Undergo Complete Blood Count (CBC) and serum ferritin testing before taking high-dose iron
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult your primary care physician to determine the underlying cause (e.g. heavy menstrual bleeding or GI blood loss).

conditions.name: Vitamin D Deficiency
conditions.description: Insufficient circulating levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D, vital for calcium absorption, bone mineralization, and immune function.
precautions: Get 15-20 minutes of midday sunlight exposure on arms and legs without sunscreen 3-4 times weekly
Consume dietary Vitamin D sources: fortified milk, egg yolks, fatty fish (salmon, mackerel), mushrooms
Get serum 25-OH Vitamin D tested through routine blood work
Take prescribed Vitamin D3 supplements under medical supervision to reach optimal levels (30-50 ng/mL)
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Consult a physician for blood level testing and appropriate oral supplementation dosing.

conditions.name: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye)
conditions.description: Inflammation or infection of the transparent membrane (conjunctiva) that lines the eyelid and covers the white part of the eyeball.
symptoms: redness in one or both eyes
watery discharge (viral/allergic) or thick yellowish crusting (bacterial)
precautions: Apply cool compresses for itching/swelling or warm compresses to loosen crusting
Wash hands frequently and avoid rubbing or touching eyes
Do not wear contact lenses until eye is fully healed
Change pillowcases daily and do not share towels or eye makeup
conditions.whenToSeeDoctor: Seek prompt eye care if experiencing severe eye pain, changes in vision, extreme light sensitivity, or copious thick pus.

faqs.question: What is considered a normal blood pressure reading versus high blood pressure?
faqs.answer:
According to the American Heart Association (AHA):
- **Normal**: Less than 120/80 mmHg
- **Elevated**: Systolic 120-129 mmHg AND Diastolic less than 80 mmHg
- **Stage 1 Hypertension**: Systolic 130-139 mmHg OR Diastolic 80-89 mmHg
- **Stage 2 Hypertension**: Systolic 140 mmHg or higher OR Diastolic 90 mmHg or higher
- **Hypertensive Crisis**: Higher than 180 and/or higher than 120 mmHg (requires immediate medical attention).

faqs.question: How can I naturally lower my blood pressure without medication?
faqs.answer:
Evidence-based lifestyle modifications include:
1. **DASH Diet**: Eating whole grains, fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy while reducing saturated fat.
2. **Sodium Reduction**: Limiting dietary sodium to under 1,500-2,300 mg per day.
3. **Aerobic Exercise**: At least 30 minutes of moderate activity 5 days a week (can lower systolic BP by 5-8 mmHg).
4. **Weight Management**: Every 1 kg (2.2 lbs) lost can lower blood pressure by roughly 1 mmHg.
5. **Limit Alcohol & Quit Smoking**: Smoking increases arterial stiffness.
6. **Stress Reduction**: Daily meditation, slow deep breathing, and quality sleep (7-8 hours).

faqs.question: What are the early warning signs of diabetes?
faqs.answer:
The classic 3 'Ps' of diabetes are:
1. **Polyuria**: Frequent urination, especially at night, as kidneys attempt to expel excess glucose.
2. **Polydipsia**: Excessive, unquenchable thirst resulting from fluid loss.
3. **Polyphagia**: Constant extreme hunger because cells are unable to utilize glucose without effective insulin.
Other early signs include chronic unexplained fatigue, blurred vision, slow-healing cuts, and recurrent yeast infections.

faqs.question: What is an HbA1c test and what do the numbers mean?
faqs.answer:
The Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) test measures the average percentage of blood sugar attached to hemoglobin over the past 2-3 months:
- **Normal**: Below 5.7%
- **Prediabetes**: 5.7% to 6.4%
- **Diabetes**: 6.5% or higher on two separate tests.
For most non-pregnant adults with diabetes, the general target is an HbA1c under 7.0%, though individual goals are personalized by a physician.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a controller inhaler and a rescue inhaler for asthma?
faqs.answer:
- **Rescue Inhalers** (e.g., Albuterol): Fast-acting bronchodilators that relax airway smooth muscles within minutes. They are used during acute flare-ups or sudden shortness of breath. They do NOT treat underlying inflammation.
- **Controller/Maintenance Inhalers** (e.g., Inhaled Corticosteroids like Fluticasone or Budesonide): Taken daily on a strict schedule to reduce chronic airway inflammation and prevent attacks. They do not provide immediate relief during an acute attack.

faqs.question: How can I tell the difference between a tension headache and a migraine?
faqs.answer:
- **Tension Headache**: Usually mild-to-moderate, feels like a tight band or dull ache wrapping around both sides of the head. Typically not worsened by physical movement and not accompanied by nausea or visual disturbances.
- **Migraine**: Moderate-to-severe, throbbing or pulsating pain, often unilateral (one side of head). Worsened by routine physical activity. Frequently accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia (light sensitivity), phonophobia (sound sensitivity), and sometimes preceding sensory/visual auras.

faqs.question: What lifestyle changes provide the best relief for acid reflux / GERD?
faqs.answer:
Key clinical recommendations for GERD management include:
1. Elevate the head of your bed by 6 inches with risers or a wedge pillow.
2. Avoid lying down for at least 3 hours after eating.
3. Eat smaller, frequent meals and avoid gorging.
4. Avoid common triggers: chocolate, peppermint, citrus fruits, tomato sauce, garlic, onions, spicy food, coffee, alcohol, and carbonated beverages.
5. Avoid tight-fitting abdominal garments.
6. Maintain a healthy body weight.

faqs.question: How do I know if I have a common cold or the flu?
faqs.answer:
- **Onset**: Flu symptoms appear abruptly (within hours), while colds develop gradually over 1-3 days.
- **Fever**: Flu often causes high fevers (100°F-102°F+), while colds rarely cause significant fever in adults.
- **Body Aches & Fatigue**: Flu causes intense, debilitating muscle aches and profound fatigue. Colds cause mild fatigue and minor aches.
- **Upper Respiratory**: Colds frequently present with sneezing, stuffy nose, and sore throat early on; flu focuses heavily on systemic exhaustion, dry cough, and fever.

faqs.question: What foods are highest in iron and how can I maximize absorption?
faqs.answer:
There are two dietary forms of iron:
1. **Heme Iron** (higher bioavailability): Lean beef, poultry, organ meats, sardines, oysters.
2. **Non-Heme Iron** (plant-based): Lentils, chickpeas, spinach, tofu, pumpkin seeds, fortified cereals.

**Absorption Optimization**:
- Pair non-heme iron foods with Vitamin C sources (citrus, bell peppers, broccoli, tomatoes).
- Avoid consuming calcium-rich dairy, antacids, green tea, or coffee during iron-rich meals, as phytates, polyphenols, and calcium inhibit absorption.

faqs.question: Can a urinary tract infection (UTI) go away on its own without antibiotics?
faqs.answer:
While very mild urinary discomfort may occasionally resolve with aggressive hydration, true bacterial UTIs typically require prescription antibiotics targeted to the offending pathogen (such as E. coli).
Leaving a UTI untreated carries significant risk of the infection ascending through the ureters into the kidneys (pyelonephritis), which can cause permanent kidney damage or systemic sepsis. If you suspect a UTI, see a healthcare provider for a urinalysis and appropriate culture-guided treatment.

faqs.question: What are the most effective treatments for seasonal allergies?
faqs.answer:
1. **Intranasal Steroid Sprays** (e.g., Fluticasone, Budesonide): Considered first-line therapy for moderate-to-severe symptoms; most effective when used consistently every day.
2. **Second-Generation Antihistamines** (e.g., Cetirizine, Loratadine, Fexofenadine): Non-drowsy oral medications that block histamine receptors.
3. **Saline Nasal Irrigation**: Gently flushes allergens and inflammatory mediators out of the sinus passages.
4. **Environmental Control**: Keep windows closed during pollen peaks, shower before bed, and use HEPA air purifiers.

faqs.question: When should someone with COVID-19 seek emergency medical care?
faqs.answer:
Seek emergency medical services immediately if you or someone you are caring for exhibits any of these warning signs:
- Trouble breathing or severe shortness of breath
- Persistent chest pain, pressure, or tightness
- New confusion or inability to wake or stay awake
- Pale, gray, or blue-colored skin, lips, or nail beds (cyanosis)
- Oxygen saturation reading below 92% on a home pulse oximeter.

faqs.question: What are the classic warning signs and symptoms of a heart attack?
faqs.answer:
The classic warning signs of a heart attack (Acute Myocardial Infarction) include:

**Primary symptoms:**
- **Chest pain or pressure**: A feeling of crushing, squeezing, tightness, or heaviness in the centre of the chest lasting more than a few minutes, or that goes away and comes back.
- **Radiating pain**: Discomfort spreading to the left arm, both arms, jaw, neck, upper back, or stomach.
- **Shortness of breath**: Often occurring alongside chest discomfort, or sometimes before it.

**Additional symptoms (especially common in women, diabetics, and elderly):**
- Cold sweats and clammy skin
- Sudden nausea or vomiting
- Lightheadedness or unexplained dizziness
- Extreme, unexplained fatigue
- Sense of impending doom or severe anxiety

⚠️ **If you or someone nearby has these symptoms, call 112 / 108 in India (or 911 internationally) immediately. Do not drive to the hospital.**

faqs.question: What is the difference between a heart attack and cardiac arrest?
faqs.answer:
These are two distinct but related cardiac emergencies:

**Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction):**
- Caused by a **blockage** in a coronary artery cutting off blood supply to the heart muscle.
- The heart continues to beat, but part of the muscle is dying.
- Patient is usually conscious and experiencing chest pain, arm pain, shortness of breath.
- **Action**: Call 112 / 108 in India (or 911) immediately. Chew aspirin if available and not contraindicated.

**Cardiac Arrest:**
- The heart **suddenly stops beating** altogether due to an electrical malfunction.
- The patient collapses, is unresponsive, and has no pulse.
- A heart attack can trigger cardiac arrest if untreated.
- **Action**: Call 112 / 108 immediately and begin CPR. Use an AED (Automated External Defibrillator) if available nearby.

faqs.question: What is the management protocol for Dengue Fever and what medications should be avoided?
faqs.answer:
- **Hydration**: Drink plenty of fluids (ORS, coconut water, soups) to prevent plasma leakage and hemoconcentration.
- **Fever Relief**: Use Paracetamol/Acetaminophen only.
- ⚠️ **Strict Warning**: NEVER take Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Naproxen, or Diclofenac, as NSAIDs thin the blood and dramatically increase internal bleeding risk in dengue.
- **Monitoring**: Check platelet count and hematocrit daily.

faqs.question: What are optimal cholesterol levels and how can LDL be reduced?
faqs.answer:
Optimal adult lipid targets:
- **Total Cholesterol**: < 200 mg/dL
- **LDL (Bad Cholesterol)**: < 100 mg/dL (or < 70 mg/dL for high cardiovascular risk)
- **HDL (Good Cholesterol)**: > 50 mg/dL (women), > 40 mg/dL (men)
- **Triglycerides**: < 150 mg/dL

To lower LDL naturally: Increase soluble fiber (oats, legumes), eliminate trans/saturated fats, exercise regularly, and avoid smoking.

faqs.question: How is PCOS diagnosed and what lifestyle habits help manage it?
faqs.answer:
PCOS is diagnosed using the Rotterdam Criteria (meeting at least 2 of 3):
1. Irregular or absent menstrual cycles
2. Clinical or biochemical signs of excess androgens (acne, hirsutism)
3. Polycystic appearance of ovaries on pelvic ultrasound

Key management habits: Low-glycemic anti-inflammatory diet, regular strength and cardio training to lower insulin resistance, weight management, and stress reduction.

faqs.question: What is a Low-FODMAP diet and how does it help IBS?
faqs.answer:
FODMAPs are short-chain carbohydrates (Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols) that are poorly absorbed in the small intestine, causing gas, bloating, and diarrhea in IBS patients.

A Low-FODMAP protocol involves:
1. **Elimination Phase (2-6 weeks)**: Cut out high-FODMAP foods (garlic, onions, wheat, dairy, apples, legumes).
2. **Reintroduction Phase**: Test individual food groups one-by-one to pinpoint exact triggers.
3. **Personalized Maintenance**: Eat a varied diet avoiding only proven triggers.

faqs.question: How long does food poisoning last and how to prevent dehydration?
faqs.answer:
Most uncomplicated viral or bacterial food poisoning episodes resolve within 24 to 48 hours.

To prevent dehydration:
- Sip Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) solution or diluted broth every 15 minutes.
- Avoid gulping large amounts of water at once (which triggers vomiting).
- Rest the stomach until vomiting ceases, then introduce the BRAT diet (Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast).
- Avoid dairy, caffeine, and fatty/fried foods for at least 48 hours.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Osteoarthritis and Rheumatoid Arthritis?
faqs.answer:
- **Osteoarthritis (OA)**: A 'wear-and-tear' mechanical breakdown of joint cartilage over time. Usually asymmetric, affects weight-bearing joints (knees, hips), and causes morning stiffness lasting < 30 minutes.
- **Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)**: A systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease where the immune system attacks joint linings. Symmetrical (both hands/wrists), causes warm red swelling, and causes morning stiffness lasting > 1 hour.

faqs.question: What is the 'Soak and Seal' method for managing eczema flare-ups?
faqs.answer:
The Soak and Seal method is the gold standard for eczema hydration:
1. Take a short, 5-10 minute bath or shower in lukewarm (never hot) water using gentle, fragrance-free soap.
2. Pat skin lightly with a towel, leaving it slightly damp (do not rub dry).
3. Within 3 minutes of stepping out, apply a thick layer of ceramide-rich ointment or moisturizing cream over the entire body to lock in moisture.

faqs.question: What is the 5-4-3-2-1 grounding technique for acute anxiety or panic?
faqs.answer:
The 5-4-3-2-1 technique interrupts panic loops by anchoring your senses to your immediate surroundings:
- 👁️ **5 things you can SEE** (e.g. clock, plant, shoe)
- ✋ **4 things you can TOUCH** (e.g. desk surface, your jacket, cold water)
- 👂 **3 things you can HEAR** (e.g. fan hum, distant cars, bird chirp)
- 👃 **2 things you can SMELL** (e.g. coffee aroma, fresh air)
- 👅 **1 thing you can TASTE** (e.g. mint, water, or clean mouth)

faqs.question: Why are antibiotics usually not prescribed for acute bronchitis?
faqs.answer: Over 90% of acute bronchitis cases are caused by viruses (such as rhinovirus, influenza, or coronavirus), not bacteria. Antibiotics only kill bacteria and have zero effect against viruses. Taking unnecessary antibiotics exposes patients to side effects (diarrhea, allergic reactions) and drives antibiotic resistance. Treatment focuses on symptom relief (hydration, humidifiers, honey for cough).

faqs.question: Why must Levothyroxine (thyroid medicine) be taken on an empty stomach?
faqs.answer:
Levothyroxine has delicate gastrointestinal absorption. Food, dietary fiber, calcium, iron supplements, coffee, and antacids bind to the hormone in the gut and severely reduce absorption.

Best practice: Take Levothyroxine with a full glass of plain water first thing in the morning, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast, coffee, or other medications.
